Definition: R1-R9 apply universally to all agents and all workflow designs; compliance requires all nine requirements to be satisfied.
I1-I10 govern all decomposition agents and must hold across conforming decomposition agents regardless of domain.
K-* invariants are enforced across the full agent suite.
Human-owned decisions are enumerated and preserved.
Task agents run without requiring mid-run human decisions.
Every agent has an explicit write scope, and tool roots are isolated from source truth.
Each run produces a new snapshot folder; snapshots and snapshot folders may not be overwritten.
Pointer files may be overwritten.
Aggregated or extracted data includes SourcePath and best-effort SectionRef.
Missing or unknown values become TBD rather than guessed.
Missing data becomes TBD; unknown values become TBD rather than guessed.
Conflicts between sources are surfaced, not silently resolved.
Pipelines have a defined brief format and deterministic outputs.
Version-control publishing is reviewable and non-destructive by default.

Synonyms: human at defined gates;human resolves at gates
Definition: The structured outline and decomposition must be confirmed by the human at defined gates.
Partitions are flat; nested partitions are prohibited.
Once assigned, IDs remain stable across revisions unless the human explicitly requests renumbering.
The production unit ID is mechanically derived from its parent partition ID.
Objectives are derived from source material; unmapped objectives are surfaced as open issues.
Non-trivial assignment decisions are recorded as explicit decisions in decomposition output.
Every decomposition includes a machine-checkable ledger and a Coverage & Telemetry summary.
Every decomposition includes a Vocabulary Map; canonical terms are used consistently, synonyms are mapped, and semantic drift is prevented.
Only humans author binding approval records.
Approvals bind to a specific git SHA.
Type 2 agent context is limited to folder contents and declared references.
Type 2 agent context has no ghost inputs.
Deliverable-local _DEPENDENCIES.md and Dependencies.csv are authoritative for dependencies.
There is no central dependency graph; aggregation is on-demand via _Reconciliation/.
Dependency references to deliverables must resolve to existing deliverable IDs.
_STATUS.md is the canonical human-readable lifecycle state file for each deliverable.
Upstream changes propagate staleness to all transitive dependent deliverables.
A deliverable is dirty if any governed input changed since its last approved SHA.
Gates are dynamic per project instance; minimum gates are seal transition and pipeline run approval.
Merge to main is allowed only when branch HEAD equals the approved SHA for the relevant run.
Claims, conclusions, and characterizations must not overstate what the available warrant supports.
Tool roots are isolated from source truth.
The enforcement map associates each enforcement point with the invariants it checks.
